correctness.rationale: The three explicit reduction identities are polynomial identities; they yield exactly a= n^2 distinct, minimal residue representatives. Their gap heights are q+9r+floor(alpha(q-Lr)/a). Since alpha(2n-1)=4a-1, adjacent residues correspond to two exact t-shifts. Each noncontributing cell is dominated by a neighboring height, and the only contributions are k(2n-3) cells of height excess 2n+2 and 2n-2 cells of excess 7(k+1). Their sum equals n^3+1 for all n=4k+3. The residue a-1, negative effective neighbor height, and k=0 are handled. An independent shortest-path verifier agrees for 21 n values; direct membership checks agree for three.

value.rationale: Isolated failures of representability with both adjacent targets representable are a natural local statistic for the three-coin linear Diophantine problem. The proof establishes an exact count over an infinite family of consecutive square denominations and a two-stratum explanation of contributions, beyond genus or conductor computations; this can inform comparisons across other residues n mod 4.
